jobs.description:
Job Description

Internship - Spring 2027 / Fall 2027 Packaging Solutions Co-op

Collaborate with Innovative 3Mers Around the World

Choosing where to start and grow your career has a major impact on your professional and personal life, so it’s equally important you know that the company that you choose to work at, and its leaders, will support and guide you. With a wide variety of people, global locations, technologies and products, 3M is a place where you can collaborate with other curious, creative 3Mers.

An internship is a temporary position within 3M. Packaging Solutions Co-ops typically work a full-time schedule throughout a 20-22 week assignment. This position is limited to working 899 hours per service credit year. 3M provides eligible interns with a housing and transportation stipend in accordance with current policy.

This position provides an opportunity to transition from other private, public, government or military experience to a 3M career.

Applications on this requisition are reviewed and filled on a rolling basis; it is in a candidate’s best interest to apply as soon as possible. Interested candidates should include a resume as part of their application.

The Impact You’ll Make in this Role

As a Packaging Solutions Co-op , you will have the opportunity to tap into your curiosity and collaborate with some of the most innovative people around the world. Here, you will make an impact by:

• Developing and implementing creative and innovative package solutions that span across all three business groups in collaboration with cross-functional team members
• Supporting the modification and improvement of existing package designs, methods and/or solutions
• Performing and coordinating package testing according to established protocols
• Working with suppliers of packaging materials and/or contract packaging vendors to obtain price/cost estimates, sample/material needs, and design requirements
• Creating, maintaining, obtaining, and analyzing packaging data that enables improvements in the packaging implementation and optimization process

Your Skills and Expertise

To set you up for success in this role from day one, 3M requires (at a minimum) the following qualifications:

• Currently pursuing a bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution
• Completed at a minimum of sophomore year (4 semesters) by the start of the internship

Additional qualifications that could help you succeed even further in this role include:

• Currently pursuing a bachelor’s degree or higher in in Package Engineering, Packaging Science, or Supply Chain from an accredited institution
• Completion of Package Materials and Package Design & Development curriculum
• Current cumulative GPA of 3.0 or higher on a 4.0 scale
• Previous experience in the packaging industry

Work location:

• Work location: This role follows an on-site working model, requiring the employee to work at least four days a week at the 3M Center in Maplewood, MN.
• Relocation: 3M provides eligible interns with a housing and transportation stipend in accordance with current policy.

Must be legally authorized to work in country of employment without sponsorship for employment visa status (e.g., H1B status).

Supporting Your Well-being

3M offers many programs to help you live your best life – both physically and financially. To ensure competitive pay and benefits, 3M regularly benchmarks with other companies that are comparable in size and scope.

Chat with Max

For assistance with searching through our current job openings or for more information about all things 3M, visit Max, our virtual recruiting assistant on 3M.com/careers.

All US-based 3M full time employees will need to sign an employee agreement as a condition of employment with 3M. This agreement lays out key terms on using 3M Confidential Information and Trade Secrets. It also has provisions discussing conflicts of interest and how inventions are assigned. Employees that are Job Grade 7 or equivalent and above may also have obligations to not compete against 3M or solicit its employees or customers, both during their employment, and for a period after they leave 3M.

Learn more about 3M’s creative solutions to the world’s problems at www.3M.com or on Instagram, Facebook, and LinkedIn @3M.

Responsibilities of this position include that corporate policies, procedures and security standards are complied with while performing assigned duties.

Safety is a core value at 3M. All employees are expected to contribute to a strong Environmental Health and Safety (EHS) culture by following safety policies, identifying hazards, and engaging in continuous improvement.

Pay & Benefits Overview: https://www.3m.com/3M/en_US/careers-us/working-at-3m/benefits/

jobs.description:
Clorox is the place that’s committed to growth – for our people and our brands. Guided by our purpose and values, and with people at the center of everything we do, we believe every one of us can make a positive impact on consumers, communities, and teammates. Join our team. #CloroxIsThePlace

Your role at Clorox

The Packaging Department Manager is responsible for supporting, leading and coordinating with the team the business production needs in the packaging area. In this role, the Packaging Department Manager will serve operational team members focusing on daily management and coordination of production, crewing, safety, quality, costs, line efficiency, people development, and performance management.

In this role, you will:

• Cultivate and drive a safety and quality mindset, culture as the TOP priority where people work together to address and act on unsafe behaviors, conditions. Ensuring all quality checks are completed acting on any variances to resolution protecting our customers and reducing plant impacts.
• Fostering a skill progression system that builds the right technical, behavioral and leadership skills across the department.
• Lead and enable effective use of Clorox systems, including SAP, EWM, and the Manufacturing Execution System (MES).
• Manage and develop LSW for your department leaders through one on one connects, coaching, and training.
• Lead Daily Management System Tier meetings and follow-up actions through team member engagement and training.
• Develop and champion a Plan-Do-Check-Act (PDCA) approach that connects department initiatives to divisional objectives and leverages Clorox 10 Manufacturing Standards.
• Actively working in conjunction and with team leadership and the Plant Operations Leader on strategic solutions and resource needs, while contributing to our people first culture.
• Develop and strengthen working relationships with plant support teams to meet targets, goals, and department needs, including Operational Excellence, Maintenance Reliability Team, Quality and Engineering.
• Support plant projects and department initiatives in partnership with Change Management, Plant Leadership, Engineering, outside contractors, and other stakeholders.
• Manage head count, overtime, weekend requirements for department based on business and budgetary needs.
• Partner and work with other department managers on overall team and plant needs, targets, labor, cost and operations day to day.
• Provide support for a 24-hour 5-day operation, including periodic off-shift work, responding to plant calls, and taking action as needed.
• Perform other duties as assigned by the manager.

What we look for

• 3+ years of experience in manufacturing and/or supply chain operations, preferably within a fast-paced manufacturing environment.
• Demonstrated people leadership experience, including directly managing teams of 10 or more employees and driving engagement, accountability, and performance.
• Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications, particularly Excel and PowerPoint, along with experience using Microsoft Teams and other business or manufacturing systems.
• Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Operations, Business, a technical discipline, or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and relevant experience.
• Strong team facilitation and consensus-building skills, with the ability to engage employees and stakeholders at various levels of the organization.
• Proven ability to lead, influence, and collaborate across functions, including working effectively with plant associates, corporate partners, contractors, Engineering, Quality, and other operational teams.
• Demonstrated ability to motivate, develop, and engage employees within a manufacturing or plant environment.
• Excellent verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to communicate expectations, priorities, and performance effectively across teams and shifts.
• Strong analytical, critical-thinking, and problem-solving skills, with the ability to identify issues, determine root causes, and drive sustainable solutions.
• Strong operational experience with exposure to continuous-improvement methodologies such as World Class Manufacturing (WCM), Lean Manufacturing, Six Sigma, PDCA, or similar structured problem-solving approaches preferred.

Workplace type:

Onsite
Our values-based culture connects to our purpose and empowers people to be their best, professionally and personally. We serve a diverse consumer base which is why we believe teams that reflect our consumers bring fresh perspectives, drive innovation, and help us stay attuned to the world around us. That’s why we foster an inclusive culture where every person can feel respected, valued, and fully able to participate, and ultimately able to thrive. Learn more .

[U.S.]Additional Information:

At Clorox, we champion people to be well and thrive, starting with our own people. To help make this possible, we offer comprehensive, competitive benefits that prioritize all aspects of wellbeing and provide flexibility for our teammates’ unique needs. This includes robust health plans, a market-leading 401(k) program with a company match, flexible time off benefits (including half-day summer Fridays depending on location), inclusive fertility/adoption benefits, and more.

We are committed to fair and equitable pay and are transparent with current and future teammates about our full salary ranges. We use broad salary ranges that reflect the competitive market for similar jobs, provide sufficient opportunity for growth as you gain experience and expand responsibilities, while also allowing for differentiation based on performance. Based on the breadth of our ranges, most new hires will start at Clorox in the first half of the applicable range. Your starting pay will depend on job-related factors, including relevant skills, knowledge, experience and location. The applicable salary range for every role in the U.S. is based on your work location and is aligned to one of three zones according to the cost of labor in your area.

–Zone A: $90,900 - $170,100

–Zone B: $83,400 - $155,900

–Zone C: $75,800 - $141,700

All ranges are subject to change in the future. Your recruiter can share more about the specific salary range for your location during the hiring process.

This job is also eligible for participation in Clorox’s incentive plans, subject to the terms of the applicable plan documents and policies.

Please apply directly to our job postings and do not submit your resume to any person via text message. Clorox does not conduct text-based interviews and encourages you to be cautious of anyone posing as a Clorox recruiter via unsolicited texts during these uncertain times.

To all recruitment agencies: Clorox (and its brand families) does not accept agency resumes. Please do not forward resumes to Clorox employees, including any members of our leadership team. Clorox is not responsible for any fees related to unsolicited resumes.

jobs.title: Packaging Engineer II, Amazon Leo
jobs.description:
LEO is Amazon’s low Earth orbit satellite broadband network. Its mission is to deliver fast, reliable internet to customers and communities around the world, and we’ve designed the system with the capacity, flexibility, and performance to serve a wide range of customers, from individual households to schools, hospitals, businesses, government agencies, and other organizations operating in locations without reliable connectivity.

Export Control Requirement: Due to applicable export control laws and regulations, candidates must be a U.S. citizen or national, U.S. permanent resident (i.e., current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum.

The LEO team is looking for an exceptional Packaging Engineer to join our team and drive standardization and efficiency for product packaging in our supply chain. The Packaging Engineer will work closely with Engineering, Global Commodity Management, Supplier Quality Management, and Operations teams in the US and abroad to define efficient, robust, and standardized packaging for our products. You will be a critical escalation path for packaging issues and work closely with partner teams to ensure cross-functional collaboration is effective.

The team is looking for knowledge in the following fields of focus:
- Clean room compliant packaging
- Manufacturing kit packaging
- Manufacturing shadow form solutions
- Transportation solutions
- Labeling and barcoding (including developing supplier standards for labeling/barcoding)
- Proven strong organizational and problem-solving skills
- Demonstrated critical thinking capability
- Enthusiasm for getting “hands on” with your team in collaborative environments
- Ability to identify risks, develop clear mitigation plans, and communicate effectively to executive stakeholders while handling multiple competing priorities in a fast-paced rapidly evolving environment

Key job responsibilities
- Partner with operations to identify packaging/labeling defects impacting operations, including safety hazards created by packaging.
- Manage the development of Packaging concepts with Packaging Vendors and Component part Suppliers, ensuring material conformity and personnel safety.
- Plan and direct activities concerned with design and development of packaging. Analyze engineering drawings and specifications of product to determine physical characteristics of component, special handling and safety requirements.
- Create detailed packaging specifications for both components and manufacturing kits, including clean room compliance.
- Define standard labeling and barcoding specifications and partner with supply chain to drive adoption by suppliers. Monitor adherence to standards and drive corrective actions as appropriate.
- Scope new technology and/or opportunities in the packaging space.

jobs.title: System Development Engineer, Robotics Delivery & Packaging Innovation (RDPI), RDPI Hardware Solutions
jobs.description:
Robotics Delivery & Packaging Innovation (RDPI) Global Engineering is looking for a System Development Engineer (SysDE) to join our New Product Introduction (NPI) team. Our mission is to eliminate operational complexity at the source, ensuring every RDPI automation solution is designed for deployability, reliability, and maintainability from Day One.

As a SysDE II on the NPI team, you will work alongside Hardware Development programs from the Alpha phase to help shape controls and system design before solutions are built. Rather than fixing deployment and reliability problems in the field, you will help design them out — contributing to the automation, firmware, and integration decisions that determine how easily a solution scales across our global network. You are a builder who designs and delivers the controls software and tooling for the systems you support, works autonomously on well-scoped problems while seeking direction on ambiguous ones, and partners with Hardware Development, Technical Program Managers, and the Scale and AI teams to deliver solutions that deploy with minimal human intervention.

This role is a strong fit for an engineer who thinks software-first and wants to grow in the software development craft. You will deepen core software engineering practices — modern languages, testing, CI/CD, and AI-native, agentic development — and apply them to industrial controls and hardware domains.

Key job responsibilities
- Contribute to NPI programs from Alpha through GA, helping influence controls and system design for deployability, reliability, and maintainability.
- Design and deliver standardized hardware/software interfaces and modular, reusable control patterns that reduce integration complexity, with guidance on the most ambiguous architectural decisions.
- Build and validate automation and commissioning frameworks (CI/CD for controls code, automated configuration validation, emulators) in partnership with the Scale team.
- Participate in reviews of architecture, design, and operations for your solutions, and incorporate feedback to raise the quality of your work.
- Partner with Hardware Development, TPMs, and the AI team to incorporate self-service deployment and predictive capabilities into solutions.
- Use AI-assisted and agentic development tools to increase the quality and velocity of your engineering work, and share what you learn with the team.
- Apply and help improve engineering and operational excellence standards, and mentor interns and junior engineers as you grow.

A day in the life
You work across industrial control platforms (Codesys, Allen-Bradley, Siemens, Beckhoff) and the networked field devices, firmware, and cloud/WMS interfaces around them. You design and build the controls software for a solution, contribute reusable control patterns to our libraries, write and review structured-text and automation-tooling code, and work with Hardware to improve a system before it's built. You take part in design reviews that surface architectural and scalability risks early, and you prototype frameworks, emulators, automated validation, and CI/CD for controls code that become the foundation future solutions are built on. You lean on AI and agentic development tools throughout — generating, testing, and troubleshooting code — so you can focus your judgment on building solutions that are correct by design.

jobs.title: Packaging Lead Engineer
jobs.description:
Packaging Lead Engineer

In this role you will be responsible for setting up the enterprise packaging strategy and technology roadmap while leading a group of engineers.

Develop, implement, and maintain comprehensive process standards and documentation to support all end-to-end packaging business and engineering workflows.

Establish packaging standards and lead execution of automation, returnable, and expendable plans while setting the standard on how Autoliv will achieve cost, quality, and sustainability goals. Assign workload to a team of engineers for new launch.

Should you be interested in overseeing these tasks and aiming for enhanced performance standards, your role will involve :

What you'll do

• Establish and maintain packaging standards for automation, returnable, and expendable execution; publish controlled specifications and playbooks

• Lead governance for exceptions/waivers; chair the standards review board and manage change control (ECO/ECN)

• Define common footprints and automation execution standards; align with safety/quality and sustainability requirements.

• Own enterprise packaging data architecture and tools (spec/PFEP, cartonization, labeling, image vaults): governance, permissions, and data-quality SLAs.

• Standardize master data (part-to-pack links, dunnage IDs, test results, sustainability attributes) and audit routines; lead training and adoption.

• Select/administer cartonization and labeling systems (GS1/AIAG compliant), including template libraries and formal change control.

• Set/enforce ID standards (serialization, barcode/QR/RFID), labeling, and traceability checkpoints (ship/receive scans, gate checks).

• Own the portfolio/roadmap for packaging materials, formats, and automation; prioritize pilots with success criteria and scale proven solutions.

• Conduct market/technology scouting; partner with suppliers/startups to mature innovations into standards.

• Develop KPIs/dashboards; monitor compliance and drive corrective actions with site leaders.

• Mentor regional teams; build capability via training, playbooks, and office hours

• Lead and set workload for a team of packaging engineers for new model launch and serialization projects

What is required

• BS in Packaging Engineering (preferred) or ME/IE

• 7–10+ years in packaging or logistics engineering, including multi-site standards/systems ownership in automotive/Tier-1 or similar high-volume manufacturing.

• Hands-on with PFEP/spec databases, cartonization (TOPS/Cape or WMS-native), labeling, and GS1/AIAG compliance.

• Experience integrating packaging data with ERP/PLM/WMS (e.g., SAP/Oracle; Teamcenter/Windchill); strong Excel/BI; familiarity with APIs/MDM concepts.

• Working knowledge of ISTA/ASTM transit testing, load-securement, and sustainability/EPR considerations.

• CAD & Packaging: SolidWorks/NX/CATIA; ArtiosCAD for corrugated/dunnage; read drawings, GD&T, basic tolerance stacks.

What’s in it for you

• Attractive compensation package

• Recognition awards, company events, family events, university discount options and many more perks.

• Gender Pay Equality

jobs.title: Senior Engineer, Packaging
jobs.location: USA - California – Irvine, United States of America
jobs.description:
Imagine how your ideas and expertise can change a patient’s life. Our Global Operations & Quality team plays a central part in ensuring our products are delivered to patients with cardiovascular disease. You’ll partner cross-functionally with manufacturing operations and sales teams, delivering thoughtful solutions to complex challenges all while developing your knowledge of the medical device industry. Whether your work includes strategic inventory planning, labeling, warehouse management, material handling, or any of our other supply chain opportunities, you will be making a meaningful contribution to our team and to patients all over the world.

This is an exciting opportunity with the World Wide Engineering team currently involved in cutting edge packaging design & development leveraging applied research in design, materials and modeling. As a Packaging Engineer you will work closely with other engineers to develop world-class capabilities and provide a competitive advantage to Edwards, through packaging design including component e.g. thermoform trays, injection molded parts, pouches and shelf & shipper boxes.

How you’ll make an impact:
• Design innovative packaging concepts for complex projects, including new product launches and existing products throughout all stages of product development from concept to launch, including clinical trials, global and limited market releases, as well as key operations initiatives.
• Develop protocols for, and implement, package design, packaging process validation, and package shelf life testing, as well as driving new packaging technologies and strategies with increased uncertainty and complexity, to improve time to market and advance the technology of package engineering at Edwards.
• Develop plans for complex projects working closely with cross-functional team members and outside suppliers.
• Validate new packaging equipment and packaging manufacturing processes to determine appropriate sourcing, purchasing, installation planning and specifications.
• Provide guidance and coaching to lower level engineers.
• Other incidental duties assigned by Leadership.

What you’ll need (Required):
• Bachelor's Degree in Engineering or Scientific field with minimum of 4 years either industry or industry/education experience or
• Master's Degree or equivalent in Engineering or Scientific field with minimum of 3 years either industry or industry/education experience.

• Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite and working knowledge of CAD software.

What else we look for (Preferred):

• Ability to effectively manage multiple priorities and deliver results in a fast-paced, cross-functional environment.

• Demonstrated ability to apply engineering principles, critical thinking, and sound technical judgment to solve complex engineering challenges.

• Strong written and verbal communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to collaborate effectively across technical and cross-functional teams (influence technical direction, resolve design, manufacturing, and quality challenges).

• Demonstrated experience independently leading packaging development and validation activities for medical devices or other highly regulated products.

• Strong understanding of design controls and the product development lifecycle for new product development.

• Demonstrated ability to develop technically sound test strategies, protocols, acceptance criteria, and reports supporting packaging design verification, process validation, and shelf-life claims.

• Working knowledge of applicable packaging standards and test methods, including ISO 11607 and relevant ASTM standards.
• Experience with environmental conditioning and distribution simulation testing, including ASTM D4332 and ASTM D4169.

• Knowledge of ASTM packaging lab test methods (e.g. peel strength, submersion leak, dye penetration, etc).

• Proven experience with material selection and design of packaging systems, including thermoformed trays, flexible pouches, lidding materials, injection-molded components, and/or corrugated/paperboard cartons.

• Strong supplier-management skills with the ability to provide technical direction and resolve design, manufacturing, and quality challenges.

• Working knowledge of statistical methods and data analysis tools (e.g. Minitab).

• Experience using Windchill PLM system or relevant PLM experience.

• Adhere to all company rules and requirements (e.g., pandemic protocols, Environmental Health & Safety, & Quality rules/guidelines) and take adequate control measures in preventing injuries to themselves and others as well as to the protection of environment and prevention of pollution under their span of influence/control.

Aligning our overall business objectives with performance, we offer competitive salaries, performance-based incentives, and a wide variety of benefits programs to address the diverse individual needs of our employees and their families.

For California, the base pay range for this position is $108,000 - $153,000 (highly experienced).

The pay for the successful candidate will depend on various factors (e.g., qualifications, education, prior experience). Applications will be accepted while this position is posted on our Careers website.

Edwards is an Equal Opportunity/Affirmative Action employer including protected Veterans and individuals with disabilities.
